scope: Proposition 6.5 (Evaluation of the cavity factor) of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every finite step quantile p, the cascade factor constructed above satisfies 1 n E log⟨W⟩p = ℓ(hp) + 1 2 ∫︂ 1 0 p(s)hp(s) ds + G1(p). (6.30) For a fixed cavity site j and a bounded continuous function ϕ, the same tilted calculation satisfies E⟨ϕ(Q12)ε1 j ε2 j ⟩p,W = ∫︂ 1 0 ϕ(p(s))Bhp (s) ds, (6.31) where Q12 is the common-level value prescribed by p and Bhp is the conditional two-spin product from Proposition 3.1. The common-level distribution itself is unchanged by the tilt.
